I've added three sets of CSS rules to ensure images are centered:

1. Base image styling:
```css
img {
  display: block;
  margin-left: auto;
  margin-right: auto;
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}
```

2. Specific container targeting (with !important to override any conflicting styles):
```css
.content img,
.sl-markdown-content img,
/* ... other selectors ... */ {
  display: block;
  margin-left: auto !important;
  margin-right: auto !important;
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}
```

3. Parent container alignment:
```css
p:has(img), 
div[class*="content"]:has(img),
/* ... other selectors ... */ {
  text-align: center;
}
```

This should ensure that all images in your main content are centered, regardless of where they appear in the document. The images will also be responsive (max-width: 100%) and maintain their aspect ratio (height: auto).

Would you like me to make any adjustments to this image centering implementation?

I've modified the click handler to:

2. Check if it's already open
   - If it is open, close it by removing the `is-open` class
   - If it's not open:
     - Close any other open sidenotes
     - Open this sidenote by adding the `is-open` class

Now in mobile view:
- First click on a number will open its sidenote (and close any other open sidenotes)
- Second click on the same number will close its sidenote
- Clicking a different number will close the current sidenote and open the new one
